item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
034
ABPZ20 KNHC 261722
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Oct 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of
Manzanillo, Mexico, and on recently downgraded Tropical Depression
Olana, located several hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston
Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 262034
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
...VANCE JOGS WESTWARD AND MAINTAINS INTENSITY FOR NOW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.4N 106.1W
ABOUT 275 MI...445 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 345 MI...555 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of Mexico
should monitor the progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 15.4 North, longitude 106.1 West. Vance is
moving toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h). A turn to the northwest 
is expected on Tuesday, followed by a northward turn on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next few days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible,
across southern Sinaloa, southwest Durango and coastal sections of
Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan.  This rainfall may produce
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern, southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 262034
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
The structure of Vance hasn't changed much since the previous 
advisory.  Visible satellite imagery is consistent with recent 
microwave fixes that the center is near the western edge of the main 
convective area.  The initial intensity will again be held at 55 kt, 
which is supported by the latest TAFB current intensity estimate and 
recent DMINT intensity estimates.

Vance has been jogging toward the west today, with the current 
motion estimated at 280/5 kt.  A slow west-northwestward track is 
expected over the next 24 hours or so due to a weak mid-level ridge 
to the north of the system.  By Wednesday, a broad mid-level trough 
near the Baja California peninsula should induce a turn toward the 
north.  The NHC track forecast has again been shifted slightly to 
the west of the previous one, and is in between the latest GDMI and 
HCCA forecasts.  It should be noted that there is considerable 
spread/uncertainty in the timing/forward speed of Vance after it 
makes the northward turn, with the HAFS and ECMWF faster to the 
north, while the GFS and GDMI show a slower northward motion.  The 
NHC forecast is a little on the slower side compared to some of the 
guidance but is faster than the GDMI.
 
Although Vance remains in a favorable thermodynamic environment with 
warm water and enough atmospheric moisture, the cyclone is 
experiencing moderate to strong west-southwesterly wind shear.  The 
wind shear is forecast to increase a bit more (to near 25 kt) by 
hour 12, and this should be enough to cause gradual to steady 
weakening over the next day or so.  On Wednesday, as Vance turns 
northward and gets closer to the broad trough over Baja California 
and the subtropical jet, the west-southwesterly vertical wind shear 
increases to over 35 kt, and is forecast to increase further on 
Thursday.  Surprisingly, most of the models hold onto this system as 
a tropical storm for a couple more days.  The NHC intensity forecast 
is similar to the previous one, and lies in the middle to lower 
portion of the guidance envelope.  It is likely that Vance's 
convection will be sheared off by 72 hours, and the NHC forecast 
shows Vance degenerating to a post-tropical remnant low around that 
time.  All of the models show the low-level circulation of Vance 
dissipating before day 4, so the timing of dissipation has been 
moved up to day 4 in the official forecast, which is before the 
circulation reaches the coast of Mexico.

Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across southern Sinaloa,
southwest Durango and coastal sections of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima
and Michoacan, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Although the wind threat to southwest Mexico is decreasing as the
forecast track shifts westward away from the coast, interests there
should continue to monitor Vance's progress.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  26/2100Z 15.4N 106.1W   55 KT  65 MPH
 12H  27/0600Z 15.6N 106.9W   50 KT  60 MPH
 24H  27/1800Z 16.7N 107.9W   45 KT  50 MPH
 36H  28/0600Z 18.1N 108.4W   40 KT  45 MPH
 48H  28/1800Z 19.8N 108.6W   40 KT  45 MPH
 60H  29/0600Z 21.3N 108.4W   35 KT  40 MPH
 72H  29/1800Z 22.6N 108.2W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 96H  30/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
